text:
eli (Finance): Brief sync 8min9  Launching a small pricing experiment for price-sheet v3 next week. Need to confirm cohort filters, grandfathering, and how we detect "surge anomalies" before flip.

maria: Can we ensure any account with an active enterprise contract is completely excluded? Also need a list of accounts with 2027+ renewal windows flagged.

aj (Billing): Exclude enterprise + reserved by default. I'll implement a hard-exclude check in the pricing runner: if account.tags contains `enterprise` or `reserved` then route to legacy rate. Also will emit a metric `billing.pricing_experiment.excluded` for auditing.

lena (Sales Ops): I'll add a `contract_renewal_year` column to the cohort CSV and push to shared drive. Which key should I use to join: `account_id` or `external_customer_id`?

aj (Billing): Use `account_id` (our canonical).

sam (Engineering): Side note: the pricing microservice caches rate tables per account for 15m. For this A/B we need cache invalidation on rollout to avoid stale rates. I can add a short TTL flush and a per-account override flag. Deploy window tomorrow 01:30 PT.

beth (Data Science): For experiment metrics we need per-account daily revenue, token counts, and a flag for vendor passed-through SKUs. I'll upload a query for DS and define the pre/post windows. Proposed canary: 3% PAYG eligible customers, randomized by account_id hash.

kevin (Revenue Ops): 3% seems fine for initial canary. I'll also add a metric to ignore cloud provider pass-through SKUs (list I'll post). We should set an alert to auto-pause the experiment if cohort median invoice change > $300/day or > 8% relative.

nora (Support): I'll prepare two macros: a neutral notification and a reconciliation promise. Also want a shared Slack snippet for account teams to paste.

eli (Finance): Question on invoicing: if we detect a surge and rollback, will we auto-credit affected customers or open a manual reconciliation? Prefer to queue credits and human-review for >$50 adjustments.

aj (Billing): Plan: automatic temporary rollback to legacy rates (no retrocredits). For any account with delta > $75/day I'll create a ticket in `#billing-reconciliations` and mark for manual review.

beth (Data Science): To detect anomalies I suggest two signals: (1) one-day absolute delta, (2) 7-day rolling z-score of per-account revenue changes. If either exceeds thresholds, trigger the pause. I'll provide SQL and thresholds this afternoon.

sam (Engineering): I'll add a feature flag `pricing_v3_ab` with cohort list and a safety circuit that listens to `billing.alerts.experimental_pause`. If triggered, feature flag flips to off automatically.

aj (Billing): Action items summary:
- lena: upload cohort CSV with `account_id` + `contract_renewal_year` (today).
- beth: SQL for anomaly detection + thresholds (this afternoon).
- sam: deploy cache invalidation + feature flag (tomorrow 01:30 PT).
- kevin: create vendor-SKU ignore list + alert (by EOD).
- nora: prepare support macros + KB (by EOD).
- aj: implement hard-exclude logic + reconciliation ticketing + PR (I'll open PR by EOD).

ops-bot: Feature flag `pricing_v3_ab` created by sam. Scheduled deploy window: 2029-04-10 01:30 PT.

maria: Uploaded `grandfathered_contracts_2029.csv` to GDrive: https://drive.internal/redwood/finance/grandfathered_contracts_2029.csv  includes `account_id`, `contract_end_date`, `legacy_rate_lock`.

eli (Finance): Great. Can we also capture the invoice-runner dry-run results and store them in the experiment doc? Ask: do we have a staging invoice-runner that mirrors production pricing?

aj (Billing): We have a staging runner. I'll execute a dry-run for the cohort and post a summary: total affected accounts, top 10 deltas, and any vendor-SKU confounds. Command: `./scripts/invoice-runner --env staging --cohort-file cohorts.csv --dry-run --output dryrun-summary.json`

beth (Data Science): Will compare cohort vs control using matched propensity (account size band) and return p-values for revenue uplift. Also will output per-account deltas for reconciliation triage.

kevin (Revenue Ops): Backup plan: if the experiment pauses, we'll keep logs and revert only the pricing_v3 toggle. No database schema changes. Good to confirm rollback is quick (sub-5min).

sam (Engineering): Rollback timeline: flag toggle is instantaneous; cache TTL flush may take ~5min to propagate worst-case. We'll monitor `billing.rate.update.latency`.

nora (Support): I'll create a KB first-draft and post the link here once ready.

eli (Finance): Final ask: please include a clear audit trail (who toggled, which accounts gated, time window) in the experiment doc. We'll need it for post-mortem and potential regulatory queries.

aj (Billing): Will add audit logs to `billing.experiments.events` and include a CSV export step in the runbook.

ops-bot: Runbook created: https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/pricing-experiment-canary.md by aj

maria: final check  go/no-go meeting tomorrow 08:30 PT in this thread. Post any last-minute blockers now.

eli (Finance): Thanks team  I'll consolidate notes and update the experiment spreadsheet.
